title: Localization sequence for equivariant coherent Grothendieck groups
statement:
For an affine finite-type group scheme $G$ over a field $F$ [def-weil-field, def-sc-group-scheme] acting on an $F$-scheme $Y$ [def-pc-scheme], a $G$-linearized coherent module means a coherent $\mathcal O_Y$-module [pqf-def-coherent] with an isomorphism $a^*\mathcal M\simeq\operatorname{pr}_2^*\mathcal M$ on $G\times_FY$, satisfying the identity and cocycle identities; its geometric fibre action is from $y$ to $gy$. Let $G_0^G(Y)$ be the abelian group on isomorphism classes of these modules, with relations $[\mathcal M]=[\mathcal M']+[\mathcal M'']$ for every equivariant short exact sequence $0\to\mathcal M'\to\mathcal M\to\mathcal M''\to0$. Let $R(G)$ be the analogous group of finite-dimensional rational $G$-modules, with multiplication induced by tensor product. Rational means a counital coassociative coaction $V\to V\otimes_FF[G]$. Tensoring a sheaf with the trivial vector bundle associated to such a module makes $G_0^G(Y)$ an $R(G)$-module. Let $Y$ now be a separated finite-type $F$-scheme [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and let $i:W\hookrightarrow Y$ be a $G$-equivariant closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion], with invariant open complement $j:U\hookrightarrow Y$ [def-weil-open-immersion]. Use ordinary closed pushforward $i_*$ as in [lem-sfb-equivariant-coherent-proper-pushforward]. Restriction and this pushforward are $R(G)$-linear, and the sequence
$$G_0^G(W)\xrightarrow{i_*}G_0^G(Y)\xrightarrow{j^*}G_0^G(U)\longrightarrow0$$
is exact: $j^*$ is surjective and $\ker(j^*)=\operatorname{im}(i_*)$. No regularity of $Y$ or $W$ is assumed; $W$ may be nonreduced or empty.

source.place: Agent-formulated supporting statement for Milne Section 22d, Theorem 22.50, printed p.480. Milne invokes a general fixed-point theorem but does not state or prove this lemma. WANTED: Thomason, Une formule de Lefschetz en K-theorie equivariante algebrique, Duke Math. J. 53 (1986), equivariant localization and devissage. No Stacks tag is asserted for this equivariant result.

proof.text: Use the action groupoid with object scheme $Y$, arrow scheme $G\times_FY$, target $a$ and source $\operatorname{pr}_2$. Its two projections are affine and flat: $G\to\operatorname{Spec}F$ is flat by [lem-pc-flat-field], affine by hypothesis, and $\operatorname{pr}_2$ is its base change; the automorphism $(g,y)\mapsto(g,gy)$ identifies $a$ with $\operatorname{pr}_2$. Explicitly on affine charts flatness is exactness of $-\otimes_FF[G]$, and localizations preserve that exactness. Affine maps are quasi-compact and quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence]. Both groupoid schemes, and $Y,W,U$, are Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], since a field is Noetherian; every open of a Noetherian scheme is quasi-compact. Invariance makes the open and closed action-groupoid morphisms Cartesian on source and target. Therefore [lem-sfb-cartesian-groupoid-pushforward-adjunction] applies to $j$ and $i$: their ordinary quasi-coherent direct images have equivariant structures and equivariant adjunction units. By [lem-sfb-groupoid-module-limits-colimits] and [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-kernel-cokernel-locnoeth], equivariant coherent modules have the underlying kernels, images, cokernels and finite sums. Restriction is exact, as its stalk maps are identities. Closed direct image is exact as its stalks are the original stalks on $W$ and zero off $W$; its coherence and identification with the stipulated group map are also [lem-sfb-equivariant-coherent-proper-pushforward].

proof.text: For a coherent equivariant module $N$ on $U$, apply [lem-sfb-equivariant-coherent-submodule-extension] to $M=j_*N$ and the identity submodule $N=j^*j_*N$. The direct image is quasi-coherent and equivariant by step 1; $j^*j_*N=N$ follows by evaluating on opens contained in $U$. We obtain a coherent equivariant extension $E\subseteq j_*N$. Thus every generator of $G_0^G(U)$ lifts. Let $H\subseteq G_0^G(Y)$ be the subgroup generated by all $[K]$ with $j^*K=0$, and put $Q=G_0^G(Y)/H$. Restriction vanishes on $H$, so induces $\bar j:Q\to G_0^G(U)$.

source.place: Agent assembly from Tags 09VH (lemma-pushforward), 077S (lemma-abelian), and coherent.tex Tags 01Y9 (lemma-power-ideal-kills-sheaf), 087T (lemma-i-star-equivalence).

proof.text: The class in $Q$ of an extension does not depend on the extension or the chosen identification on $U$. Indeed, given extensions $E,E'$ and an equivariant isomorphism $h:j^*E\simeq j^*E'$, extend its graph, a coherent equivariant submodule of $j^*(E\oplus E')$, to $L\subseteq E\oplus E'$ by [lem-sfb-equivariant-coherent-submodule-extension]. Each projection $p:L\to E$ or $E'$ restricts to an isomorphism. Its kernel and cokernel are coherent equivariant modules supported on $W$ by step 1. The two short exact sequences through $\operatorname{im}p$ give $[L]-[E]=[\ker p]-[\operatorname{coker}p]\in H$ and the same formula for $E'$. Hence $[E]=[E']$ in $Q$.

source.place: Agent assembly from Tags 09VH (lemma-pushforward), 077S (lemma-abelian), and coherent.tex Tags 01Y9 (lemma-power-ideal-kills-sheaf), 087T (lemma-i-star-equivalence).

proof.text: The assignment $[N]\mapsto[E]\bmod H$ respects every defining short exact relation on $U$. For $0\to N'\to N\to N''\to0$, choose any extension $E$ of $N$ from step 2. Extend the submodule $N'\subseteq j^*E$ to $E'\subseteq E$ by [lem-sfb-equivariant-coherent-submodule-extension]. Then $E/E'$ is coherent equivariant and restricts to $N''$ by step 1, so $[E]=[E']+[E/E']$. Independence from step 3 proves the required relation for any choices of extensions. We obtain a homomorphism $b:G_0^G(U)\to Q$. It is inverse to $\bar j$: restriction of an extension is its original module, and every coherent equivariant module on $Y$ is itself an extension of its restriction. Thus $\ker j^*=H$.

proof.text: Let $I$ be the ideal of $W$. For every generator $[K]$ of $H$, its support lies in $|W|$, so [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-support-power-ideal-kills] gives $I^nK=0$ for some $n\geq0$. The ideal $I$ is equivariant: it is the kernel of the equivariant map $\mathcal O_Y\to i_*\mathcal O_W$ of step 1. Its powers and the submodules $I^rK$ are preserved by linearization, since the two flat pullbacks preserve images of multiplication. These images are quasi-coherent by [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-tensor-product-affine-sections] and [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-module-cokernel-image], and coherent as submodules of $K$ by [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-kernel-cokernel-locnoeth]. The finite filtration has coherent equivariant quotients $Q_r=I^rK/I^{r+1}K$ annihilated by $I$.

source.place: Agent assembly from Tags 09VH (lemma-pushforward), 077S (lemma-abelian), and coherent.tex Tags 01Y9 (lemma-power-ideal-kills-sheaf), 087T (lemma-i-star-equivalence).

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-coherent-equivalence] (1), write $Q_r\simeq i_*A_r$ with $A_r$ coherent on $W$. The linearization descends: pull back along $a$ and $\operatorname{pr}_2$, use their Cartesian squares with $i$ and the degree-zero isomorphisms of [lem-pc-flat-base-change-cohom] to view the linearization of $Q_r$ as an isomorphism between closed direct images on $G\times_FY$. Full faithfulness of the same closed-immersion equivalence gives a unique isomorphism on $G\times_FW$. Its identity and cocycle equations follow by faithfulness after direct image on $W$ and $G\times_FG\times_FW$, respectively. Thus $A_r$ is equivariant. The filtration relations give $[K]=\sum_{r=0}^{n-1}[Q_r]=i_*\sum_r[A_r]$; if $n=0$, $K=0$ and the sum is empty. Hence $H\subseteq\operatorname{im}i_*$. Conversely $j^*i_*A=0$ on every open in $U$, so $\operatorname{im}i_*\subseteq H$. Together with steps 2 and 4 this proves exactness, without replacing $W$ by its reduction.

proof.text: Finally $j^*(M\otimes_FV)=(j^*M)\otimes_FV$ for every finite-dimensional rational $G$-module $V$. Also $i_*(A\otimes_FV)\simeq(i_*A)\otimes_FV$: in a basis of $V$ both sides are the same finite sum of the underlying sheaf, and the basis-free map on sections $a\otimes v\mapsto a\otimes v$ commutes with the diagonal linearizations. Tensoring with $V$ is exact since it is a finite sum locally, and similarly exact sequences of $F$-representations remain exact after tensoring a sheaf (they split as $F$-vector spaces). Thus both maps commute with the actions of representation generators and hence with $R(G)$. If $W=\varnothing$, $I=\mathcal O_Y$ and the only supported coherent module is zero; if $U=\varnothing$, every coherent module is covered by the same finite filtration argument. The construction also permits $Y=\varnothing$, nonreduced $W$, and nonsmooth $G$.
